emptyProjects: Add a folder and Pulso reads its commands.
noManifest: Pulso found nothing to run here. It reads:
manifestWarnings: Some manifests could not be read
manifestBroken: One of its project files is not valid.
manifestUnreadable: One of its project files could not be opened.
projectMissing: This folder is no longer there.
errorNotADirectory: That is a file, not a folder.
errorUnreadable: That folder could not be read.
errorInvalidInput: Pulso did not understand that value.
errorStorage: Pulso could not save the change.
overviewLede: What is running right now, and what you launch often.
processesLede: Everything Pulso started this session, alive or finished.
settingsLede: Preferences for the window and the menu bar.
showInPopover: Show in the menu bar again
onlyInstalled: Only what is installed on this Mac appears here. The default is chosen in Settings.
noEditors: No editor was found on this Mac.
nothingSelected: Pick a run and its details appear here.
noFilesRead: No file has been read yet.
openStoredLog: Read the output this run saved
environmentFine: Every program these commands need resolves.

environmentMissing.one: {count} program could not be found, which is what a “command not found” looks like.
environmentMissing.other: {count} programs could not be found, which is what a “command not found” looks like.

logRetention: up to {count} lines; older output is discarded
confirmStopBody: {label} will be asked to stop, and killed if it does not.
themeHint: Dark, light, or whatever the system is using.
themePaletteHint: Pulso's own colours, or a theme you already know.
languageHint: Applies to the window and the menu bar.
transparencyHint: macOS material behind the main window. The menu bar menu always uses the system menu material.
soundCuesHint: One sound when something long finishes well and another when something fails. Several at once sound as one.
openAtLoginHint: Pulso starts in the menu bar, with no window.
defaultEditorHint: What ⌘O opens, and what the project header hands the folder to.
keepRunningHint: The processes live in Rust, not in this window.
confirmStopHint: Worth it when something has been running for hours.
logLinesHint: Past the cap, the oldest lines are dropped first.
notifyOnFailureHint: A macOS notification when a command fails, if the window is not in front.
notifyOnReady: Notify when a server is ready
notifyOnReadyHint: When a process opens its first port. Several starting together send one notification.
notifyOnDoneHint: When a command that ran over 20 seconds finishes well, like a build or the tests.

projectsMissing.one: {count} stored, {missing} with no folder on disk.
projectsMissing.other: {count} stored, {missing} with no folder on disk.

importedNothing: Nothing new: everything in the file was already in Pulso.
projectsTransferHint: The file carries the projects, their flags, your commands and the groups.
sessionLogHint: One file with the settings and this session's output, for reporting a problem.

executionHistoryHint.one: {count} run, with the last 200 lines of each.
executionHistoryHint.other: {count} runs, with the last 200 lines of each.

confirmClearHistoryBody: Runs from earlier sessions go, along with the output they saved. Anything still running is left alone.
shortcutOpenEditor: Open the project in the editor
hintPorts: TCP listeners · refresh every 3 s while visible
portsLede: Verified TCP listeners on this Mac, including processes outside Pulso.
searchPorts: Search by port, process, PID or project…
portsDesktopOnly: Open Pulso desktop to inspect real ports on this Mac.
portsUnavailable: Ports could not be read. Try refreshing.
openPortHttpHint: Try HTTP on loopback. A listening port is not necessarily a web server.
portProtected: System, other-user and Pulso's own processes cannot be stopped here.
confirmPortStopTitle: Stop the process holding this port?
confirmExternalPortStopBody: Send SIGTERM to {process} (PID {pid}) holding port {port}? All sockets belonging to that process may close. Pulso will not stop its process group or force-kill it.
confirmManagedPortStopBody: Stop the Pulso command containing {process} (PID {pid}), holding port {port}? Its whole process group will stop, with the usual forced cleanup if needed.
portStopRequested: Stop requested for {process} (PID {pid}). It is still listening; no forced stop will be sent to an external process.
portsNote: Read with macOS lsof every 3 s while this section is visible. Only TCP LISTEN sockets visible to your user are listed; no elevated permissions. Stopping always asks for confirmation. External processes receive SIGTERM only and are never stopped when Pulso quits.
homeFolderHint: Leave blank to run in your home folder (~).
projectFolderHint: Leave blank to use the project folder.
menubarFavorite: Show as a favorite in the menu bar
shellCommandHint: Commands that require interactive input are not supported.
noCustomCommands: Your commands, ready when you need them
customCommandsEmpty: Save a command like brew upgrade. Use your home folder, a project, or another folder.
deleteCommandBody: Delete “{label}”? Its saved command will be removed.
hintCommands: Favorites are in the menu bar too
designReviewHint: Actions are simulated; no real processes or data are changed.
catalogLede: Everything Pulso can run: what it found in your projects and what you wrote yourself.
confirmStopAllBody: They will be asked to stop; any that do not answer are terminated.
samplingNote: CPU and memory are sampled every 2 s, only for processes Pulso started.
launchEmpty: Star a command with ★ to keep it at hand here.
welcomeBody: Pulso reads its scripts, Makefile and the rest, and lets you run them from here or from the menu bar.
deleteGroupBody: Delete the group “{label}”? The commands stay as they are.
groupPick: Pick the commands and put them in the order they should start.
groupsEmpty: Group the commands you start together, like api, web and database, and run them with one click.
groupMissing: A command in this group no longer exists.
